text: Lessons 16 and 17 covered the outbound half of email: a trigger fires, a template fills in, the recipient gets a message. Inbound Email Actions handle the other direction entirely — what happens when that recipient hits Reply. When a caller replies to an update about their incident, ServiceNow has to figure out which record the reply belongs to, and then decide what to do with it, and both of those are governed by records on the sysevent_in_email_action table.

ServiceNow can't just guess which Incident a reply is about. The real mechanism is a watermark — a hidden reference embedded in the outbound notification, typically in the body or subject, that most email clients quote back below a reply automatically. When an inbound email arrives, ServiceNow scans for that watermark, and finding it tells the system definitively which record the reply is actually about, instead of trying to parse a subject line a user may have edited or stripped entirely.

Once a record is matched, an Inbound Email Action defines what actually happens to it. A real, common example: take the body of the reply and add it as a work note, or a comment if it came from the end-user side, on the matched Incident. The action is scoped to a table and carries a script with the inbound email's subject, body, and sender available to it — the deeper scripting itself is covered properly later in this path.

Inbound Email Actions aren't all the same shape. A Record Action runs against a record the system has already matched via watermark. Separately, processing distinguishes a genuine Reply, matched to an existing record, from a Forward, which changes what context is reliably available, from a New inbound email with no watermark match at all — which can still create a brand-new record, like turning a support-inbox email into a fresh Incident.

None of this watermark-and-matching machinery is visible to the end user. They just see that replying to an email about their ticket updated the ticket, and that invisibility is the entire point — a natural path for someone who lives in their inbox, not a service portal, to add information to their own record without logging in at all.

Getting the action's script right, appending cleanly rather than duplicating quoted text or overwriting existing notes, is what keeps that experience trustworthy instead of messy. Next up: the Notifications Lab, putting triggers, templates, and inbound actions together for one real, worked scenario.
